corrected_value.title: Counterfactual thinking and victim compensation: A test of norm theory.

decisions.location: Abstract; Introduction, Choice of studies for replication; Results, Part 3: convenience-store robbery scenario; References (line 1)
decisions.quote: Part 3 is a replication of Experiment 1 from Miller and McFarland (1986) with the robbery-scenario – the study that meant to provide the ﬁrst empirical test of norm theory.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this request. The full text explicitly states and executes a three-part replication across two experiments: Parts 1 and 2 replicate the hitchhiker and car-accident scenarios from Kahneman and Miller (1986, Psychological Review, 93(2), 136-153, 10.1037/0033-295x.93.2.136), which is present as shipped row 1660, whereas Part 3 directly replicates Experiment 1 (the between-subjects convenience-store robbery victim compensation scenario) from Miller and McFarland (1986, 'Counterfactual thinking and victim compensation: A test of norm theory', Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 12, 513-519). Miller and McFarland (1986) is an independent original empirical paper that is absent from all shipped rows. No DOI is printed in the source text.
